description: Recorded tool-call script for ECII Test D (a standalone design object), replayed by the FAKE provider. It proves the structure only: a standalone intent has no system gaps and no research items, so nothing is asked and nothing is researched. It is not a model run and says nothing about reasoning quality. Domain words appear here as fixture values only.

turns.user: ^Design a freestanding drill-bit organizer for my workbench

arguments.rationale: The organizer stands on its own on a surface and does not attach to or exchange anything with another system.
objectives: Keep drill bits sorted and visible on a workbench
arguments.reason: ECII Test D: interpret the intent before designing

steps.final: I interpreted this as a standalone design object: it does not integrate with another system. Apply the intent to record it.

Gaps: ${conceptualize.identify_gaps.data.counts.essential} essential, ${conceptualize.identify_gaps.data.counts.concept} concept. No system gaps and nothing to research, so I will continue without asking.

arguments.text: Standalone ways to organise a freestanding organizer
arguments.name: Organizer architectures

alternatives.name: Tiered rack with drilled slots
alternatives.summary: Stacked tiers, each with a row of slots.

advantages: No interface to any other system
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Items stand upright in slots in stepped tiers
architecture.loadPath: Weight rests on the work surface through the base
architecture.installationRemoval: Place on the surface; nothing to install
evidenceRequired: Number and size of the items to store

alternatives.name: Magnetic strip with clips
alternatives.summary: A strip holds items along a edge.

advantages: No interface to any other system
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Items held along a strip by magnetic attraction
architecture.loadPath: Weight is carried by the strip and its fixing
architecture.installationRemoval: Screw the strip to a wall or stand
evidenceRequired: Mass of the items and a mounting surface

advantages: No interface to any other system
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Items in radial slots on a rotating disc
architecture.loadPath: Weight rests on the base through a central bearing
architecture.installationRemoval: Place on the surface; the disc lifts off
disadvantages: More parts than a fixed rack
evidenceRequired: Number of items and the reach of the person

steps.final: Because the organizer works alone, there is no host interface to identify. I prepared three standalone architectures: a tiered rack, a magnetic strip and a rotating carousel. Apply to record them.
